definitions.explanation: A person's skill level or capacity to accomplish something, often evaluated in a professional or competitive context. Implies proven or demonstrable ability.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{力量|りきりょう}は{確|たし}かだ。
{指導者|しどうしゃ}としての{力量|りきりょう}が{問|と}われている。
examples.english: His competence as a leader is being questioned.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトを{成功|せいこう}させるには、チーム{全体|ぜんたい}の{力量|りきりょう}を{底上|そこあ}げする{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: To make this project succeed, we need to raise the overall capability of the team.

notes: Common collocations: {力量|りきりょう}が{問|と}われる (one's ability is tested/questioned), {力量|りきりょう}を{発揮|はっき}する (to demonstrate one's ability), {力量|りきりょう}{不足|ぶそく} (lack of ability). Often used when assessing someone's suitability for a role or task. Related: {能力|のうりょく} (ability — more general), {実力|じつりょく} (real ability — emphasizes what someone can actually do vs. credentials), {手腕|しゅわん} (skill/prowess — emphasizes practical skill in handling matters).
